senses.definition: (superlative) Most-liked. (In other words, [person]'s favorite [noun] = the [noun] that [person] likes the most.)
examples: I saw a hilariously funny movie with all of my favourite comedians in it.

quotes.text: The Nanny is one of Pippa's favourite shows, but tonight the pleasure of mindlessly blobbing out in her usual Sunday-laid-back-luxury style...

Then there are the characters Rudd describes as “the full-on buffoons”, such as reporter Brian Fantana in Anchorman, who gives names to his testicles and – still my favourite Rudd performance – Andy the obnoxious summer camp counsellor in cult 2001 comedy Wet Hot American Summer, which is being revived on Netflix this summer, in which Rudd will co-star alongside original cast members including Poehler and Bradley Cooper.

quotes.text: What joy has this dog in miſchief!—More than I can have in the completion of my moſt favourite purpoſes!

senses.definition: A person or thing who enjoys special regard or favour.
examples: The teacher's favourite always went first.

senses.definition: A person who is preferred or trusted above all others.
A contestant or competitor thought most likely to win.
examples: You were my favourite to win the spelling competition.
She's the favourite, she'll probably be elected.

quotes.text: Netherlands, one of the pre-tournament favourites, combined their undoubted guile, creativity, pace and attacking quality with midfield grit and organisation.

senses.definition: (Internet) A bookmark on a web browser or website.
(in the plural) A short curl dangling over the temples, fashionable in the reign of Charles II.

quotes.text: the Favourites hang loose upon the Temples with a languishing Lock in the middle

senses.definition: (Internet) To add to one's list of favourite items on a website that allows users to compile such lists.
